title: Two-minute escalation pocket scratch
content:
Purpose: quick, scannable escalation & triage notes for bridge handoffs. Keep this on the watch tablet — two-minute read to understand what to do, who to call, and the minimal fixes that actually work (not academic troubleshooting).

Shift snapshot template (copy into handoff message):
- Window: 22:00–06:00 PT (local)
- Current primary region: us-west-2 (fallback eu-west-1)
- Active incidents: none / <short summary>
- Major deploys in last 4h: model-rollout v1.8 -> v1.8-q8 (canary 10%)
- Known flappers: kvcache-writer (see notes below)
- Oncall: Maya (me) -> next: Ravi (pager)

Live quick-check checklist (first 90s)
1) Alerts dashboard quick glance (Console > Alerts > Last hour): any P99 token latency spikes?
2) k8s pods: kubectl get pods -n inference --selector=app=serving -o wide | grep CrashLoopBackOff
3) Serving errors: curl -s "https://obs.example/api/errors?hours=1" | jq '.errors | length' (fast count)
4) Queue backlog: redis-cli -h redis-prod llen request-queue
5) Billing/usage blip? Quick usage run: curl -s "https://billing.internal/usage?window=1h" | jq '.tokens'

Two-step triage for common incidents (aim: action in <5 minutes)
A) High token latency (P99 > 800ms)
  Step 1 (fast): Check autoscaler: kubectl get hpa -n inference serving-hpa -> pending? If scaled to 0, trigger scale: kubectl scale deployment/serving --replicas=3 -n inference
  Step 2 (if persists): Fast-fallback to quantized variant: POST /api/v1/route/override {model:my-model-v1-q8} (use Console quick-run) and notify on #sre-bridge

B) Model OOMs / SIGKILL on GPU node
  Step 1: Drain affected node: kubectl cordon <node>, kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data -n inference
  Step 2: Re-route heavy traffic to dedicated fallback pool (dedicated-fallback-1) via routing override in Console. If no capacity: notify infra and request temporary burst allocation (pager).

C) Upstream datastore latency (redis > 150ms)
  Step 1: Flip cache-miss mitigation: enable short-circuit serving mode (ENV: SHORT_CIRCUIT=1) using console quick-toggle
  Step 2: If redis cluster unhealthy, fail open to read-replica: route READS to redis-replica-read-1. Escalate to DB owner if write errors observed.

Escalation matrix (who to call — order matters)
- Level 1 (oncall SRE): Ravi Kumar (pager), Slack @ravi — first 10m
- Level 2 (runtime infra): Sofia Martinez, mobile -> call +1-415-555-0190 then Slack @sofia if no ack in 8m
- Level 3 (platform lead/exec): Priya Rao (email and pager) — only for cross-region outages or SLA breaches

Quick commands (clipboard friendly)
- Restart serving deployment: kubectl rollout restart deploy/serving -n inference
- Push routing override (curl): curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' -d '{"route":"fallback"}' https://console.internal/api/route
- Inspect GPU usage: nvidia-smi dmon -s u -o DT

Known flappers / gotchas (short notes)
- kvcache-writer: rotates nightly at 03:00 and sometimes leaves behind stale lock files; quick fix: rm /var/lib/kvcache/lock.* && systemctl restart kvcache-writer
- gateway-proxy: recent config change introduced 30s connection timeouts for streaming; workaround: set STREAM_TIMEOUT=60 in proxy env until a proper rollout (PR#678) lands
- model-pin mismatch: Canary machine may use quantized variant while autoscaler expects fp16; check model metadata (Console -> Models -> version metadata) if you see tensor shape mismatch errors

Temporary procedures (for this watch)
- If Canary rollout causes >1% error increase in serving: immediately rollback canary to previous route (Console -> Rollouts -> Revert canary) and set a Jira ticket with logs pinned.
- If dedicated pool saturates: enable burst capacity (Console -> Dedicated -> Burst -> +2gpus) and set an incident note (time, reason, top callers).

Post-incident capture (fill this into the incident note)
- Time window: start / end
- Trigger/alert that started it
- Concrete action taken (commands, overrides, who was paged)
- Root-cause hypothesis (brief)
- Next steps / owners (Jira ticket link)

Handoff quick lines (what I leave next oncall)
- Anything unresolved (1–3 bullets) with a clear owner. Example: "kvcache-writer stale-lock - owner: infra-kv (Ravi) - TODO: deploy cleanup script before 03:00"
- Planned deploys in next 4h: list them with risk note
- Any muted alerts and why

Personal reminders (for me)
- Keep fix commands short and logged in the incident note. Avoid long ephemeral hacks without follow-up.
- If you call Level 2, paste the console trace link in the pager alert — saves 5+ minutes.

Open TODOs during this watch (copy into handoff)
- Add automated check to detect stale kvcache lock files (infra ticket created)
- Verify STREAM_TIMEOUT PR#678 tests on canary cluster

End — quick footer: 2-min rule: if you can resolve in 2 minutes with low risk -> do it and note; otherwise escalate. This doc lives in my watch tablet; rename and expand if you steal it.

---
Scratch log (raw, chronological entries)
2024-11-06 23:12 — saw P95 bump to 420ms; scaled deployment to 3 replicas -> P95 dropped to 170ms. Left note in incident log.
2024-11-07 02:48 — minor redis latency spike, enabled SHORT_CIRCUIT=1, relayed to DB oncall (Sofia).
2024-11-07 03:10 — kvcache cleanup executed manually, left follow-up infra ticket.

Notes-to-self: keep this slim. Turn common 2-step triages into first-responder checklist snippets in Console.
